classification.difficultyReason: Divide by twelve and interpret the quotient as completely filled boxes and the remainder as unpacked balls; both interpretations are explicitly requested.

content.prompt: There are 542 tennis balls to be packed into boxes of 12. How many boxes will be filled and how many tennis balls will be left over?

answer.short: 45 boxes will be filled; 2 tennis balls will be left over.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{array}{r}\hphantom{000}\hspace{0.9em}\underline{\hphantom{0}\hspace{0.9em}\hphantom{0}\mathllap{4}\hspace{0.9em}\hphantom{0}\mathllap{5}\hspace{0.9em}}\\
\hphantom{000}\mathllap{12\big)}\hspace{0.9em}\hphantom{0}\mathllap{5}\hspace{0.9em}\hphantom{0}\mathllap{4}\hspace{0.9em}\hphantom{0}\mathllap{{}^{6}2}\hspace{0.9em}\end{array}$$

$542\div12=45\text{ remainder }2$.

45 boxes will be filled, with 2 tennis balls left over.
